chunks: From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, who said:
I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'When you evening comes, and you see the sun setting and turning away, then say:'
'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Praise is to Allah Who did not take a son, and there was no partner for Him in the Kingdom.'
Praise is to Allah Who is described and cannot be described, and He knows and cannot be fully known. He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the chests conceal.

I seek Refuge with the Noble Face of Allah and by the Great Name of Allah from the evil of what He spread and created, and from the evil of what is beneath the earth, and from the evil of what is apparent and what is hidden.

And from the evil of what was in the night and the day, and from the evil of Abu Murra (Satan) and what he begot, and from the evil of the Allurements, and from the evil of what I have described and what I have not described.
So praise is to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
He mentioned that it is a safety from the predatory beasts and from the Pelted Satan and from his offspring.
He said: 'And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: When you morning comes,'
'Glory be to Allah, the King, the Holy,' three times.

'O Allah! I seek Refuge with You from the decline of Your Bounties, and from the changing of my health, and from the suddenness of Your Wrath, and from the attainment of wretchedness, and from the evil of what preceded in the Book.'
'O Allah! I ask You by the Might of Your Kingdom and the Intensity of Your Strength, and by the Magnificence of Your Authority, and by Your Power over Your creatures.'
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended morning and evening supplications in Shia tradition for protection and gratitude?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* outlines the ritual of *Adhkar* (remembrances) for morning and evening, emphasizing the transition of time as a moment for spiritual protection (*aman*) from both visible and hidden evils, including Satan and beasts. The Imam’s supplication highlights God’s transcendence (*tanzih*) and omniscience, while Ali’s morning prayer underscores reliance on divine power to ward off sudden calamities and the permanence of decree (*al-katb*), reflecting key Shia theological concepts of *tawhid* and *ma'ad*.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Abdul Rahman Bin Hammad, from Abdullah Bin Ibrahim Al Ja’fary who said, 
‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Whenever evening comes, so look at the sun in the west and its setting, so say, ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Beneficent, the merciful.
The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who did not Take a son and there does not happen to be an associate for Him<sup>azwj</sup> in the Kingdom.

The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who Describes and cannot be described, and He<sup>azwj</sup> Knows and cannot be known. He<sup>azwj</sup> Knows the treachery of the eyes and what the chests conceal.

I seek Refuge with the Benevolent Face of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and by the Magnificent Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, from the evil of what is spread and settled, and the evil of what is beneath the surface, and from the evil of what is apparent and what is hidden, and from the evil of what was in the night and the day, and from the evil of Abu Murra (Satan<sup>la</sup>) and what he<sup>la</sup> begot, and from the evil of the allurements, and from the evil of what can be described and what cannot be described.
So the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the worlds’.
He<sup>asws</sup> mentioned that it is a safety from the predatory animals and from the Pelted Satan<sup>la</sup>, and from his<sup>la</sup> offspring<sup>la</sup>’.
Heasws said: ‘And it was so that Amir Al-Momineenasws was saying: ‘Whenever it is morning, (say), ‘Glory be to Allahazwj, the King, the Holy’, three times. ‘O Allahazwj!

I seek Refuge with You<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> from the decline of Your<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Bounties, and from the changing of my good health, and from the sudden afflictions, and from the lowliness of the wretchedness, and from the evil of what preceded in the Book.

O Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>! I ask You<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> by the Mightt of Your<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Kingdom and the Intensity of Your<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Strength, and by the Magnificence of Your<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Authority, and by You<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> power over Your<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> creatures’.
en.sarwar: 30. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Ja’fari who has said the following:
“I heard abu al-Hassan (a.s.) saying, ‘In the evening when you see the sun is disappearing say, ‘
(I begin) in the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. All praise belongs to Allah, Who has no children, never had a partner in the kingdom,
all praise belongs to Allah Who describes things and Himself is beyond description, knows and is not known. He knows the secret glance of eyes and what hearts hide.
I seek protection with Allah’s honorable face, with Allah’s great name against the evil of what He has spread and settled, the evil under the ground, the evil of what is manifest or hidden,

the evil of things in the night and during the day, the evil of abu Murrah (Satan) and what he has given birth to, the evil of false emotional attraction, the evil of what I mentioned and what I have not mentioned.
All praise belongs to Allah, Cherisher of the worlds.’
The Imam said, ‘It is protection against beasts, Satan condemned to be stoned and his offspring.’
Amir al- Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) would say in the morning,
‘Glory belongs to Allah, the King, the Most Holy, three times,

O Lord, I seek protection against my loss of Your bounties, change in good health that You have given. Your sudden displeasure, the approaching of misfortune, and the evil of what came to pass in the book.
O Lord, I plead before You through the majesty of Your kingdom, the intensity of Your power, the greatness of Your domain and Your power over Your creatures.’”
